scientific_question: Which additional 2026 Tier-B memory methods have source code whose identity can be frozen for a future same-protocol WMA adapter, without substituting similarly named projects?
decision_informed: Whether Hindsight, Memory-R1, APEX-MEM, or ACL-2026 LightMem may enter source materialization and adapter-feasibility work.
scientific_evidence_role: bibliographic identity and source-availability evidence only; no adapter, lifecycle, numerical, superiority, or SOTA claim is eligible

candidates.paper_identity: Hindsight: Structured Agent Memory that Retains, Recalls, and Reflects; ACL 2026 System Demonstrations
candidates.common_track_hypothesis: Text/caption-mediated WMA lifecycle may map retain to completed sessions and recall to retrieval; reflect must not replace the common WMA answer generator.
candidates.unresolved_before_adapter: The official system uses PostgreSQL/pgvector and multiple retrieval channels; exact embedded-versus-service deployment and model calls require source audit.

candidates.evidence: The repository README identifies the paper and authors but states that code is coming soon; the observed tree is not accepted as a runnable method implementation.
candidates.next_check: A future discovery snapshot may re-evaluate a new immutable commit, but this record cannot be upgraded based on the paper's reported numbers.

candidates.evidence: The official ACL paper and its metadata expose no verifiable code repository in the audited source surface.
candidates.inference_boundary: This is absence of a verified source at the observation time, not proof that no private or later repository exists.

candidates.paper_identity: Lightweight LLM Agent Memory with Small Language Models; Jiaquan Zhang et al.; ACL 2026

rejected_name_collision.repository_identity: LightMem: Lightweight and Efficient Memory-Augmented Generation; Jizhan Fang et al.; ICLR 2026
rejected_name_collision.reason: The title, author list, venue, method description, and paper identity differ from the registered ACL-2026 method. A shared short name is not sufficient source provenance.

hindsight_source_materialization.wave1_non_interference: Source-only acquisition may run while Wave-1 is active only after a read-only check confirms ample storage and no process references the fresh target or evidence root. It may not install, build, start PostgreSQL, load a model, call an API, or use a GPU.

acceptance: The checkout resolves exactly to the frozen Hindsight commit and official origin.
The worktree is clean, has no submodules, no Git LFS pointer, and no tracked model-like weight file.
Every tracked path is a regular non-symlink file with retained bytes and SHA-256.
At least one tracked license file identifies the MIT License.
The tracked worktree stays below the frozen byte ceiling.
The evidence root is TERMINAL_ACCEPTED without TERMINAL_REJECTED and its evidence inventory verifies.
failure: Any collision, source identity mismatch, dirty tree, submodule, symlink, LFS pointer, model-like weight, missing MIT license, byte-ceiling violation, network error, or timeout seals TERMINAL_REJECTED and preserves the partial checkout. No in-place repair or automatic retry is allowed.
next_gate_after_acceptance: Independently audit the Hindsight source tree, package/deployment boundary, retain/recall APIs, persistence, model calls, and license before designing an adapter. Source acceptance never authorizes environment, service, lifecycle, or numerical execution.
prohibited_actions: using the Memory-R1 placeholder repository as runnable code
substituting zjunlp/LightMem for the distinct ACL-2026 LightMem identity
inventing an APEX-MEM repository or importing its reported scores into local-result cells
starting Hindsight dependencies, PostgreSQL, pgvector, models, API calls, lifecycle checks, or numerical evaluation
editing or deleting a terminal source root in place
populating a numerical comparison-table cell from this stage
